title: Context fragility traffic sweep (8k/32k/128k)
summary: This working note captures the design, prompt sets, and regression outcomes for a traffic-sweep style evaluation of long-context and retrieval interactions across 8k, 32k and 128k profiles. Focus is on context fragility under interleaved retrieval bursts, truncation alignment when retrieval tokens exceed client slice budgets, and attention sink symptoms when repeated retrievals re-reference large prefixes. The doc collects reproducer snippets, metric definitions, and prioritized remediation candidates.
objectives: 1) Surface deterministic failure modes that only appear under heavy interleaved retrievals or after repeated prefix replays. 2) Measure truncation point variability across sequence-length-aware tokenizers and our runtime preemption. 3) Quantify attention-sink impact on tail-latency and factual fidelity when retrievals chain back into the same context window. 4) Produce regression signal hooks (prompt-surface tests + unit metrics) for CI.
test-matrix: Matrix axes: model_variant (open-v1, opt-quant, redwood-compat), context_profile (8k, 32k, 128k), retrieval_pattern (single-shot, burst-3, interleaved-10), retrieval_size (100, 1k, 5k token chunks), request-concurrency (1, 8, 32), kv-cache-policy (none, prefix-only, full-kvcache), routing (local, fallback). Each cell executed N=50 end-to-end conversations with seeded RNG. Primary metrics captured: truncated_token_count, prefix_coherence_score (BLEU-like against oracle), attention_sink_indicator (ratio of attention mass on stale prefix tokens), p50/p95/p99 latency, token-cost, fidelity-regression-rate (manual eval sample).
prompt-samples:
We constructed three canonical probes:
1) Referential chain probe (R-Chain): user asks a 3-step reasoning question where each step requires retrieving an earlier doc excerpt; retrievals return overlapping long passages that cause the model to replay prefixes. Example:
--system: You are a technical assistant.
--user: Step A: read doc X and state its key constraints. Step B: given X, describe affected APIs. Step C: summarize how B changes a deployment plan.
Retrievals return document fragments of 2k-6k tokens.

2) Adversarial truncation probe (Trunc-Ad): feed a single 128k prompt composed of alternating instructions and retrieval snippets sized to push the client-side slice window to a non-boundary point; then append a 64-token critical instruction expected to be kept. We check whether the final instruction is present in model context post-truncation.

3) Attention-sink probe (Sink-Loop): repeated retrievals that re-introduce the same 700-token vendor legal paragraph ten times at different offsets, then ask a factual question referencing a single sentence inside the paragraph. Measure whether the model uses the most recent occurrence or conflates earlier copies.
methodology:
- Orchestration: harness built on top of the evaluation runner (eval-runner v0.9) with deterministic retrieving via synthetic index (controlled shard).
- Tokenization: tests run with both BPE and SentencePiece tokenizers to detect tokenizer alignment issues.
- Retrieval simulator: configurable latency and jitter added to the retrieval channel to exercise prefetch and backpressure logic.
- KV cache toggles: we forced cold-start, warm-start, and eviction-at-threshold scenarios to expose regeneration glitches.
- Human eval: stratified random sample of 200 responses across failure cells annotated for fidelity and hallucination.
- Failure classification: truncated_missing_instruction, hallucinated_entity, stale_reference, coherence_degradation, latency_falloff.
- Repeats: 5 run seeds per cell, checks for flaky vs persistent failures.
metrics-summary:
Key aggregated observations across all runs:
- Truncation variability: on 32k profile under Interleaved-10 with 5k retrieval chunks, 23% of sessions lost the final critical instruction (Trunc-Ad). On 8k profile this spikes to 48%. On 128k it falls below 2%.
- Prefix coherence: R-Chain average prefix_coherence_score fell by 11 pts when retrieval_size >= 1k and kv-cache-policy==prefix-only (evidence of prefix replay mismatches).
- Attention sink indicator: Sink-Loop produced a 3.6x increase in attention mass on earlier copies vs latest when the runtime reused cached key/value shards older than 6 requests. This correlated with 17% factual answers referencing older text.
- Latency: p95 token latency increased 2.3x under burst-3 retrievals on dedicated pools with conservative batching enabled.
- Cost delta: quantized variants reduce token-cost by ~22% but increased truncation sensitivity (likely due to sequence packing heuristics).
notable-failures:
1) Reproducer JIRA-ML-4123: deterministic missing instruction after two interleaved retrieval bursts on 8k profile. Steps to reproduce included in reproducer-instructions. Likely root cause: preemptive slice eviction + off-by-one in slice boundary computation.
2) Stale-kv misalignment: repeated prefix replays cause model to attend to earlier positions because runtime reused an lru-sharded KV entry with stale position offsets; manifested as 'older copy wins' in Sink-Loop.
3) Tokenizer boundary split: certain UTF-8 heavy documents caused off-by-one tokenization which, after compression and packing, pushed critical tokens past truncation margin.
4) Quantized packing regression: quantized model runtime packs more aggressively which sometimes leads to earlier truncation under identical token budgets.

Each failure includes a proposed hotfix: numerical boundary patch, kvcache invalidation at retrieval-chain start, tokenizer normalization pass, and conservative packing toggle for quantized models.
reproducer-instructions:
Minimal reproducer (local dev):
1) Checkout branch: github.com/redwood-inference/evals refs/qa/context-fragility-repro
2) Start eval-runner: python runner.py --profile 8k --pattern interleaved-10 --retrieval-size 5000 --seed 42
3) Ensure retrieval simulator seeded (scripts/simulate_index.py --seed 42) and that kvcache toggles enabled (ENV KVCACHE_POLICY=prefix-only).
4) Run with logs at DEBUG; look for 'slice-evict' events in runtime logs and compare returned context hash with client-side expected hash.
5) Attach traces and a sample pair to JIRA-ML-4123.

Notes: we have an automated repro script under /infra/tests/context-fragility-sweep that packages a tarball for oncall shares.
remediation-recommendations:
Short-term (P0/P1):
- P0: Patch off-by-one in slice boundary calc and roll forward to canary (infra PR ready).
- P0: Invalidate kvcache entries tied to retrieval-chain start to ensure latest offsets are used.
- P1: Add tokenizer normalization for high-UTF8 docs in the ingestion pipeline (pre-tokenize check).
- P1: Add a conservative packing flag for quantized runtime and experiment with a 1.05x safety margin on token budgets.

Medium-term:
- Add a synthetic CI job that runs the Trunc-Ad probe against every model onboarding change (smoke on 8k/32k).
- Expand attention-sink instrumentation: emit per-request attention mass histogram and expose a regression alert when mass on stale positions > 2x baseline.
- Explore adaptive eviction: warm-start heuristics that prefer most-recent retrieval contexts for replayed keys.

Long-term:
- Rework kvcache metadata to store logical timestamps and retrieval-chain IDs so that reuse decisions are aware of sequence causality.
- Integrate retrieval index checks into prefetching to avoid duplicate heavy inserts that cause sink patterns.

notes:
Working doc: rough drafts of findings above. Some hypothesis rows still unvalidated — see 'open-questions' below. Preserve seeds and raw trace bundles when closing this doc.

human_notes:
Annotator feedback: human raters found 72% of 'lost instruction' cases lead to downstream chain failures rather than recoverable hallucinations — i.e., once an instruction is truncated the rest of the response becomes nonsensical. Manual annotations available in BENCHMARKS/2025-11/human-annotations.csv.

Quick wins: add 1) a pre-send prefix-length guard in the SDK to warn when combined retrieval+prompt > profile soft-limit and 2) a debug flag that dumps effective context slice to logs for failing sessions.
conclusion: There are actionable fixes that should reduce the majority of failures observed in the sweep. Priorities: slice-boundary patch and kvcache invalidation are high-impact and low-effort. Adding Trunc-Ad to onboarding CI will prevent regressions. Instrumentation for attention-mass should follow to catch subtle sink regressions early. This doc is ready for engineering review and assignment.
